$comment: Content-Type -> cache file extension, and the extension back to the Content-Type a
cache HIT is served with. Read by BOTH implementations of the shared tile cache:
They write into the same directory layout ({source}/{z}/{x}/{y}.{ext}) on purpose, so
the mapping is not free to differ: a tile the CLI files as .png is later read back by
the C# proxy and served with the Content-Type this table gives for 'png'. The TS side
used to pass a hardcoded 'png' at the store site regardless of what came back, so every
JPEG the CLI cached was served to a browser as image/png.
Unknown / absent content types fall back to png, matching what the C# switch does with
its default arm — a wrong extension is recoverable, refusing to cache is not.
